title: Distributed Safety Critical Control among Uncontrollable Agents Using Reconstructed Control Barrier Functions
venue: 2026 European Control Conference (ECC)
evidence: Sec. III-C: a per-agent QP minimally modifies the nominal input so the reconstructed CBF holds, acting as a safety filter among controllable and uncontrollable agents (pedestrians, human-driven vehicles) to avoid inter-agent and obstacle collisions.
method: Distributed adaptive observer estimates other agents' states; coupled CBF is reconstructed on estimates with a prescribed-performance adaptive offset so reconstructed constraint implies the true one; CBF-QP safety filter per agent.
evaluation: Single simulation: 4 robots (1 uncontrollable), 3 obstacles; no baselines; qualitative trajectories, CBF values and inputs only; no hardware or solve time reported.
contribution: Fully distributed CBF-QP safety filter that reconstructs coupled barrier constraints from observer estimates, provably keeping a multi-agent system safe among uncontrollable agents.
flag: Borderline E2: evaluation is one illustrative simulation with no baselines or quantitative safety metrics; theory-first paper. No latency or compute figures. Simulation shows an input u4 for the 'uncontrollable' robot.

title: FORMULA: FORmation MPC with neUral barrier Learning for safety Assurance
venue: 2026 IEEE Intelligent Vehicles Symposium (IV)
evidence: Sec. III-B/IV-C: the learned NN-CBF is linearised at the current state and the MPC-CLF command is projected onto it via a minimum-deviation QP, so the safety filter overrides the nominal input to keep multi-robot formations collision-free.
method: Distributed MPC with CLF constraints for formation tracking, neural-network CBF (2x64 MLP) learned from sampled states as a decentralised safety filter, plus event-triggered deadlock resolver that perturbs the reference.
evaluation: Simulation only, 2D cluttered workspace, 3/5/9 unicycle robots; baselines APF, MPC-CBF, CLF+CBF-QP; safety rate, formation error, min distance (single rollouts); no timing or hardware reported.
contribution: Learning-enhanced distributed MPC that combines CLF formation tracking with a learned neural barrier safety filter, raising safety rate over APF, MPC-CBF and analytic CLF+CBF-QP baselines in simulation.
flag: Claims 'real-time feasibility with formal safety guarantees' but reports no compute times, control rates or hardware, and the NN-CBF is only trained on sampled states (no verification). Table I uses single rollouts. No real robots.

title: Game-Theoretic Safe Multiagent Motion Planning With Reachability Analysis for Dynamic and Uncertain Environments
venue: IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics
evidence: Sec. III-C/V: a multi-agent forward reachable set (ellipsoidal error sets under bounded disturbance) is added as an exponential penalty so 'the MA-FRS penalties enforce non-overlapping safety regions'; deployed onboard Raspberry Pi 5 vehicles with per-step latency below the 0.2 s control period.
method: Decentralised motion planning as a dynamic potential game; neighbourhood-dominated iterated best response with epsilon-Nash convergence; reachability (MA-FRS) soft penalties for uncertainty-aware collision avoidance within receding-horizon MPC.
evaluation: Sim: 3-15 quadrotors, 50 MC runs, noise sweeps; baselines w/o-RE-DPG, PiLQR, Swarm-DRL; tracking cost, time efficiency, collision ratio. Real: 3-4 4WD vehicles on Raspberry Pi 5, <0.2 s/step, FRS 46-102 ms.
contribution: Reachability-enhanced dynamic potential game planner that adds multi-agent forward reachable sets as collision penalties, lowering collision ratios versus PiLQR and Swarm-DRL and running onboard Raspberry Pi 5 ground vehicles.
flag: Criterion (d) is borderline: onboard latency (<0.2 s, equal to control step) is reported but no explicit deadline analysis. Collision avoidance is a soft cost penalty, not a hard constraint or interception, despite abstract wording. Real experiments are 2D only (abstract says 2D and 3D). Extended version of the TII paper; check for duplicate record.

title: IDCAIS: Interdefender Collision-Aware Interception Strategy Against Multiple Attackers
venue: IEEE Transactions on Control of Network Systems
evidence: Sec. IV-A: when collisions cannot be avoided by the collision-aware assignment or attackers deviate from time-optimal play, an exponential-CBF QCQP adds a minimal correction delta-u to each defender's nominal control to keep defenders more than the collision radius apart.
method: MIQP defender-attacker assignment weighting time-optimal capture time against predicted inter-defender collision time (Algorithm 1 pre-filter); exponential CBF QCQP minimally corrects defender controls when collisions remain.
evaluation: MATLAB simulations, 2v2 and 3v3 damped double integrators; baseline CUDAA (collision-unaware); inter-defender distance, capture/escape outcomes; 68% collision avoidance over 20 configs; collision-time computation 61-1057 s for 15-30 attackers; no hardware.
contribution: Collision-aware defender assignment via MIQP plus an exponential-CBF minimal control correction that avoids inter-defender collisions during multi-attacker interception where collision-unaware assignment fails.
flag: Multi-agent hazard is inter-defender collision only; evaluation is scenario-based with one small statistic (68% over 20 configs). No forward-invariance proof (safety analysis deferred to future work); reported compute times are seconds to minutes, so not real-time. arXiv 2021, journal version 2026.

title: Manifold-constrained Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability Learning for Decentralized Multi-Agent Motion Planning
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
evidence: Sec. IV.C: the receding-horizon planner requires the learned HJ reachability value function, evaluated pairwise against each other agent, to stay above a safety buffer, and falls back to a conservative collision-evading control if the optimisation fails.
method: Manifold-constrained Hamilton-Jacobi reachability learned with a DeepReach-style solver; value function used as pairwise safety constraint in decentralized min-max receding-horizon trajectory optimisation (HaMMAR).
evaluation: Sim 2D ablation plus 2-5 UR5 manipulation tasks, 100 cases each; baselines Opt w/o HJR, AtlasRRT (dec./cent.); success, collision, planning time 0.10-0.17 s/step on Xeon w5-2455X + RTX 4070; 5 real-robot trials.
contribution: Learns manifold-constrained HJ reachability value functions and uses them as pairwise safety constraints in decentralized receding-horizon planning for multi-robot manipulation, with a conservative fail-safe fallback.
flag: Criterion (a) is via fail-safe fallback inside the planner, not a standalone filter; no explicit latency constraint (~100 ms/step on desktop GPU); offline HJR training time not reported.

title: Matrix Control Barrier Functions
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control
evidence: Sec. VII-C/VIII-A: nominal tracking commands of five UAVs are passed through a CBF-SDP safety filter enforcing a matrix barrier (network connectivity LMI) plus pairwise collision CBFs, solved at every state update.
method: Matrix-valued control barrier functions for safe sets given by semidefinite/indefinite matrix inequalities; continuous CBF-SDP safety filter, also yielding continuous filters for Boolean (OR) barrier compositions.
evaluation: Five-quadrotor connectivity maintenance in sim and Crazyflie 2.1+ hardware (OptiTrack); qualitative vs scalar eigenvalue CBF (chattering); Clarabel SDP solve 1-2 ms on Ryzen 9 9950X at 240 Hz, offboard.
contribution: Extends control barrier functions to matrix inequalities, giving continuous SDP-based safety filters for nonsmooth and disjunctive safe sets, demonstrated on multi-UAV connectivity maintenance in hardware.
flag: Multi-agent filter is centralized and offboard; 1-2 ms solve time is reported but no explicit latency constraint is posed (criterion (d) not claimed); no quantitative baseline metrics.

title: Mean-Field Control Barrier Functions for Stochastic Multi-Agent Systems
venue: IEEE Control Systems Letters
evidence: Sec. II, Theorem 1 and Eq. 15: the nominal mean-field control field is corrected by a QP to lie in the admissible set guaranteeing forward invariance of the density-level safe set, keeping agents out of dangerous regions.
method: Mean-field control barrier functions for Fokker-Planck dynamics of stochastic multi-agent populations; QP correction of the control field with bounded-stability guarantee for density tracking.
evaluation: Numerical particle sims (720-820 agents) of coverage and shepherding, 50 runs each, baseline nominal controller only; metric fraction of agents in dangerous/goal regions; no hardware or runtime reported.
contribution: Derives mean-field control barrier functions for stochastic multi-agent densities governed by Fokker-Planck equations, with a QP safety correction and bounded stability under safety intervention.
flag: Density-level (mean-field) abstraction, simulation only, no timing or latency data; only baseline is the unfiltered nominal controller.

title: Multi-Robot Trajectory Planning via Constrained Bayesian Optimization and Local Cost Map Learning with STL-Based Conflict Resolution
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
evidence: Sec. IV, Alg. 2: for each robot pair an STL monitor is fed the pairwise state at each timestep and a conflict is recorded when robustness is negative, replacing the geometric collision test of K-CBS; conflicts are then resolved in the high-level search.
method: Two-stage multi-robot planner: cBOT single-robot sampling with GP-learned local cost/feasibility and constrained expected improvement; STL-KCBS conflict detection/resolution via STL robustness monitoring.
evaluation: Four sim environments, 2-50 robots, 10 trials, nine+ baselines (K-CBS/RRT/STGCS variants); success, runtime, path length; i7-10700 CPU; 3-robot indoor (42 ms) and 2-3 ASV lake trials.
contribution: Combines GP-guided constrained Bayesian sampling for single-robot kinodynamic planning with STL-monitored conflict detection and resolution for scalable, probabilistically complete multi-robot planning.
flag: Borderline E1: primarily an offline coordination planner; the safety element is STL-monitored inter-robot conflict detection, not runtime interception; no execution-time replanning loop; no human-in-the-loop.

title: R3R: Decentralized Multi-Agent Collision Avoidance with Infinite-Horizon Safety
venue: 2026 American Control Conference (ACC)
evidence: Sec. III-C/Def. 10: a candidate trajectory is committed only if it passes a validity check (safe set, backup set reached, >=delta from neighbours' backup sets, R-bounded, avoids neighbours' committed trajectories); otherwise the agent keeps tracking its previous committed trajectory, giving infinite-horizon collision-free guarantees among asynchronously replanning agents (Thm. 1-2).
method: Decentralized asynchronous gatekeeper: nominal-plus-backup candidate trajectories validated against neighbours' committed trajectories; R-Boundedness ties planning radius to communication radius (R_comm = 3R_plan + delta) for infinite-horizon safety.
evaluation: Julia simulation, 8-128 Dubins vehicles, swap/city/willow-garage maps; baseline nonlinear MPC (Ipopt); metrics safety and success (100%/97-100%); avg 1.4 ms replan step, M2 MacBook Air; no hardware.
contribution: Decentralized gatekeeper with R-Boundedness certifies infinite-horizon collision avoidance for asynchronously replanning agents using only range-limited local communication, with per-step cost scaling in local density not team size.
flag: Safety mechanism is a commit-or-fallback shield (a) in a multi-agent collision setting (c); latency reported (1.4 ms avg) but no deadline/jitter model, no edge hardware, no handoff. Runtime of 32-agent case only; non-ideal networks deferred to future work.

title: Self-Navigation in Non-Adversarial Crowds: An Invariant Set-Based Approach
venue: IEEE Transactions on Control Systems Technology
evidence: Sec. III.A-B: at each planning instance the robot selects, from LiDAR returns of non-coordinating agents, the largest invariant disc that no static or constant-velocity moving point can enter within 1/f_p, then applies an input-constrained controller whose sublevel set is that disc (Thm. 1-2); Sec. IV.A reports ~57 ms per planning instance on a Raspberry Pi 4.
method: Input-constrained feedback controller for unicycle robots with disc-shaped invariant sublevel sets; per-cycle onboard LiDAR search for the feasible invariant disc nearest the target among non-coordinating moving agents.
evaluation: MATLAB multi-agent simulation (no collisions); 5 TurtleBot3/RPi4 with LiDAR, ViCON; baseline decoupled plan-and-react; metrics path length, curvature; ~57 ms/plan on RPi4; up to 3x parallel speedup on workstation.
contribution: Invariant-set-based reactive controller lets non-holonomic robots navigate crowds of non-coordinating agents from onboard LiDAR alone, with ~57 ms per planning cycle on a Raspberry Pi 4.
flag: Borderline (c)/E4: multi-agent only in that other agents are sensed obstacles with no coordination; multi-agent safety is empirical, formal result is single-robot invariance. Not a runtime monitor/deferral mechanism. Human appears only as an obstacle. arXiv title differs slightly from venue title (adds 'Non-Adversarial').

title: Stop Means Stop: Measuring and Repairing the Enforcement Gap in Agent-Framework Control Primitives
venue: IEEE Access
evidence: Sec. 5.1/5.3: SOUNDGATE requires every side effect to be submitted for admission at the tool boundary and executes it only on a release verdict; gated effects are held until an authenticated operator DECIDE, rejection is sticky, and cancelled/timed-out runs' effects are fenced; Sec. 4.2: 215/1,200 live runs leaked unmediated vs 0/1,200 through SOUNDGATE.
method: External Rust effect gate below the framework scheduler: hold-until-decided approval, sticky rejection, dedup-on-replay, fence-on-cancel; core verified with Verus, TLA+/TLC, TLAPS, Loom plus differential conformance.
evaluation: Six agent frameworks (LangGraph, LlamaIndex, MS Agent Framework, OpenAI Agents SDK, CrewAI, LangGraph.js); 1,000 random workflows, 1,200 live runs across 4 LLMs, injection tests, tau-bench; leak rate, false refusals (0); ~1 ms/gated write, 12k-26k admissions/s; hardware not retrieved.
contribution: Shows that human-approval gates, cancellation and timeouts in six LLM-agent frameworks fail to block parallel-branch side effects, and repairs this with SOUNDGATE, a verified effect gate adding ~1 ms per write with zero false refusals.
flag: Strong fit for (a) runtime interception, (c) safety evaluation of tool-calling agents, (e) human approval gates. Section 6 (performance hardware, p99 latency, tau-bench detail) could not be retrieved via WebFetch truncation; numbers taken from abstract/Sec. 4. Single author; v3 of a preprint, check for other queued versions.

title: TopoEvo: A Topology-Aware Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Framework for Root Cause Analysis in Microservices
venue: 2026 IEEE International Conference on Web Services (ICWS)
evidence: Sec. III.D: a Hypothesis Planner, Metric/Log/Trace agents and a Judge agent run a Hypothesis-Evidence-Test workflow to separate initiating anomalies from amplified downstream symptoms; Sec. III.E: memory and test-time adaptation; no interception, halting or remediation of actions is described, only post-hoc diagnosis.
method: Topology-aware RCA: GAT localizer over service graph, VQ symptom tokens, multi-agent LLM Hypothesis-Evidence-Test workflow, self-evolving memory and test-time adaptation under topology drift.
evaluation: AIOps Challenge HipsterShop benchmark and a production incident dataset; baselines Nezha, Eadro, HolisticRCA, TAMO, RCAgent, mABC; ACC@1/3/5 (75.66% vs 72.22%); GPT-4o, A100 80GB; latency metric defined but not reported.
contribution: TopoEvo diagnoses microservice root causes under cascading failures and topology drift by combining graph-based localization, symptom tokens and a multi-agent hypothesis-testing LLM workflow with self-evolving memory.
flag: Multi-agent LLM pipeline for offline root cause analysis; cascading failures are diagnosed after the fact, no runtime safety interception, deferral, latency constraint or handoff. Multi-agent only as an analysis workflow (protocol v1.2). Nearest overlap is graph representation of service dependency state (b, weak).

title: WinkTPG: An Execution Framework for Multi-Agent Path Finding Using Temporal Reasoning
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
evidence: Sec. IV adds safety margins to Type-2 (passing-order) timing constraints under bounded/Gaussian delay models so collision-free precedence is kept at execution; Sec. V WinkTPG replans every t_e s from reported reach times.
method: Kinodynamic Temporal Plan Graph (kTPG) turns a MAPF plan into speed profiles via 1-D SIPP-IP; uncertainty margins on precedence constraints; windowed online replanning from reported agent states.
evaluation: Six MovingAI maps up to 1,000 agents vs ADG and KDN; suboptimality, success, violation rate, runtime; AMD 3990x single core, ~344-519 ms per round at 1,000 agents; Isaac Sim + 6 JetBots.
contribution: WinkTPG executes multi-agent path-finding plans as kinodynamic speed profiles with delay-robust precedence margins and windowed replanning, keeping 1,000 agents collision-free with sub-second per-round planning.
flag: v1.5: MAPF execution planner; no runtime monitor; safety not primary claim. Borderline (c): collision safety comes from precedence margins and replanning, not a runtime monitor or halt; maintainer to judge whether MAPF execution robustness counts as a safety mechanism (protocol v1.2). No edge/deadline claim; 1 s figure is per planning round on a server CPU.

title: A Fairness-Oriented Control Framework for Safety-Critical Multi-Robot Systems: Alternative Authority Control
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
evidence: Sec. IV.A: Flexible CBF models each non-authority robot as a velocity-scaled, velocity-oriented ellipse and enforces the discrete condition dh >= -gamma*h at every MPC step (Eq. 25f) so the authority robot avoids the others.
method: Alternative Authority Control rotates planning authority among robots (round-robin plus proximity-triggered tree search); authority robot runs MPC with Flexible-CBF constraints treating others as moving obstacles; Bayesian tuning offline.
evaluation: Simulation: search-and-rescue robots and 15-vehicle lane-change scenario vs LFC-MPC-FCBF (priority by index); task duration, computation time (39-541 ms vs 183-4025 ms), min distance, infeasibility rate; hardware unspecified.
contribution: Rotating planning authority among robots and a velocity-aware flexible control barrier function inside MPC gives fair, scalable multi-robot collision avoidance with zero QP infeasibility where a standard CBF fails.
flag: v1.5: CBF inside MPC; primary claim is fairness/coordination. Safety is a CBF constraint inside each robot's MPC, not a separate interception layer. Paper has internal inconsistencies (text percentages vs Tables I-II, stray '13' entries); 'real-world scenario' has no hardware details, appears simulation-only.

title: A Learning-Based Control Barrier Function for Car-Like Robots: Toward Less Conservative Collision Avoidance
venue: 2025 European Control Conference (ECC)
evidence: Sec. III-E (Eq. 23): at each time step a QP minimally perturbs the nominal RL controller's action subject to the second-order CBF constraint Psi_2 >= 0 to 'verify the safety of this nominal controller'; Theorem 3 gives forward invariance of the pairwise safe set.
method: Neural network approximates a non-differentiable heading- and shape-aware safety margin between two car-like robots in relative coordinates; conservative CBF h = h_theta - eps; QP safety filter over an RL policy.
evaluation: Numerical simulation, two robots, overtaking and bypassing vs circle-based centre-to-centre margin; lateral evasion (33.5% less), completion time, QP solve 7.6 / 11.6 ms per step (CVXPY, hardware unspecified).
contribution: A learned, shape- and heading-aware control barrier function lets a QP safety filter wrap an RL driving policy with provable pairwise collision avoidance and 33.5% less conservatism than circle-based margins.
flag: Multi-agent only nominally: pairwise ego/other formulation, two robots in experiments, k-robot extension (Remark 4) untested and scalability listed as future work. Reported approximation error inconsistent (2.76% vs 1.4%). No edge or deadline claim.

title: A Modular Safety Filter for Safety-Certified Cyber-Physical Systems
venue: 2025 IEEE Conference on Control Technology and Applications (CCTA)
evidence: Sec. III (Eq. 9, Algorithm 1): the add-on filter receives the possibly attacked command u_a(t) and state x(t) and outputs the 'nearest safe input' u_s(t) whose predicted N-step trajectory stays admissible and ends in a terminal safe set; Sec. IV adds inter-robot collision constraints for 20 robots (Eq. 15).
method: Modular predictive safety filter: finite-horizon optimisation projects the received actuator command onto the set of inputs with a feasible backup trajectory to an invariant terminal set; detector- and controller-agnostic.
evaluation: Simulation only (CasADi): 20 unicycle robots in circular formation under covert intelligent and FDI attacks during t in [5,10] s vs unfiltered system; qualitative collision/admissibility plots; no runtime or hardware; filter Ts = 0.02 s.
contribution: A plug-in predictive safety filter certifies a 20-robot formation against actuator and sensor cyber-attacks by replacing any received command with the nearest input that keeps a feasible backup trajectory to a safe rest set.
flag: v1.5: runtime filter but qualitative figures only, no metric or baseline. Centralised filter over stacked 20-agent state; assumes zero transmission delay and deterministic dynamics; evaluation is qualitative figures with no metrics, compute time or hardware. Earlier version was arXiv v1 (2024) - check for a later journal extension.

title: A Rapid Trajectory Optimization and Control Framework for Resource-Constrained Applications
venue: 2025 American Control Conference (ACC)
evidence: Sec. IV: 'The objective is to dock a chaser TPODS to a stationary target'; collision avoidance is a soft keep-out correction (DCOL scale factor s re-solved below s_thr=1.5) inside the MPC, deployed on a Teensy 4.1 with 512 kB RAM.
method: MPC via Integral Chebyshev Collocation (MPC^3): finite-horizon QP with constant Hessian/constraint matrices, soft input/velocity limits, DCOL keep-out correction, warm start, auto-generated embedded code.
evaluation: 1-DoF/multi-DoF double integrator and CubeSat docking sim; baseline discrete MPC (OSQP); run time and memory vs horizon/state dim on i5 PC (MATLAB) and Teensy 4.1; 500 Monte Carlo noise runs; no ms latency figures in text.
contribution: Chebyshev-collocation MPC whose memory and run time do not grow with horizon, enabling embedded CubeSat docking with soft collision keep-out on a 512 kB microcontroller.
flag: Abstract mentions 'multi-agent space systems' but body is single chaser vs stationary target; edge/resource-constrained MPC relevant to (d) only loosely (no explicit latency constraint or safety-decision framing); collision correction is a controller constraint, not a safety reflex. Borderline (d).

title: AVOID-JACK: Avoidance of Jackknifing for Swarms of Long Heavy Articulated Vehicles
venue: 2025 IEEE International Symposium on Multi-Robot and Multi-Agent Systems (MRS)
evidence: Abstract/Sec. IV-C: a 'purely reaction-based, decentralized swarm intelligence strategy' for swarms of heavy articulated vehicles that prevents jackknifing and, when two HAVs are in potential collision, replaces goal vectors by 'vectors directed away from each other'; 99.7% of two-HAV runs collision-free.
method: Decentralized attraction-repulsion steering: articulation-weighted repulsion (w_jack=1+tanh(b-c cos delta)) against jackknifing, Dubins-path goal attraction, circle-based mutual evasion, speed cap derived from reaction distance.
evaluation: Simulation only; 4,500 single-HAV and 4,500 two-HAV randomized runs (1-10 trailers, dt=0.2 s); no baselines; metrics: jackknife rate, goal hits, potential/actual collisions; no hardware or compute times.
contribution: A decentralized reactive swarm rule for long articulated trucks that avoids jackknifing in ~99% of randomized runs and mutual collisions in 99.7% of two-vehicle runs, without central coordination.
flag: v1.5: metrics but no baseline or ablation; multi-agent nominal. Multi-agent only nominally in experiments (max two HAVs); no baselines; stability rests on untested Assumption 2; no latency or real-world results; real-robot tests listed as future work.

title: Anomaly Detection in Cooperative Vehicle Perception Systems Under Imperfect Communication
venue: 2025 22nd International Conference on Ubiquitous Robots (UR)
evidence: Sec. 3.1: 'The key problem in this study is the joint classification of anomalous behavior within a group of vehicles that remain under communication range'; a GAT spatial fusion over a fully connected vehicle graph plus a temporal transformer detects zigzag, sudden braking/turning, lane switching and tailgating in 6-agent MetaDrive scenes under communication blackouts.
method: CPAD: graph attention layers over per-timestep vehicle graph (lidar, lane, side sensors), global mean pooling, transformer encoder over time, attention pooling, sigmoid anomaly classifier.
evaluation: Modified MetaDrive, 6 agents, 15,000 scenarios/90,000 rule-labelled trajectories; baselines LOF, LSTM, decision tree, SP-AE; F1 0.70, AUC 0.90; F1 drops to 0.58-0.61 at 25% blackouts; no hardware or latency reported.
contribution: A graph-attention plus temporal-transformer detector that jointly classifies anomalous driving across a connected group of vehicles and degrades gracefully under simulated communication loss.
flag: Detection only: the override/consensus use case in Sec. 1 is not implemented; real-time claims are qualitative with no measured latency; synthetic rule-based labels; (b) is partial (classification over multi-agent graph, not prediction).

title: AttentionSwarm: Reinforcement Learning with Attention Control Barrier Function for Crazyflie Drones in Dynamic Environments
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Biomimetics (ROBIO)
evidence: Sec. III.A/III.D: 'two Bitcraze Crazyflie drones operating in an environment with a moving obstacle and a gate'; MAPPO where 'we replace the traditional Lagrangian multipliers with an Attention-based Control Barrier Function' so attention weights 'serve as safety penalties' for collision avoidance.
method: Centralized MAPPO-Lagrangian variant: attention over obstacle features produces CBF-parameter weights that scale a cost-advantage safety penalty in training; -100 collision reward; KL trust region.
evaluation: gym-pybullet-drones sim and indoor Crazyflie 2.1 flights with Vicon; training on i9/RTX 4090; racing 100%/95% success (1/3 obstacles, 15 runs); landing vs SafeSwarm 87% vs 80% success; no inference latency reported.
contribution: Multi-agent PPO for Crazyflie swarms in which an attention-based control-barrier term replaces Lagrangian multipliers, yielding collision-free racing and landing around a moving obstacle in sim and indoor flight.
flag: CBF is a learned soft training penalty, not a runtime filter/shield, despite 'formally guarantee safety' wording; only two drones; 'real-time' claim has no latency numbers; Table II comparison text misreports precision vs success rate; drone-game results in abstract only.

title: Collision Avoidance for Ellipsoidal Rigid Bodies With Control Barrier Functions Designed From Rotating Supporting Hyperplanes
venue: IEEE Transactions on Control Systems Technology
evidence: Sec. IV-B: each of n ellipsoidal rigid bodies solves a distributed QP that minimally modifies its nominal input subject to the rotating-supporting-hyperplane CBF constraint, using poses and hyperplane parameters shared via communication; Sec. V-C demonstrates sixteen bodies.
method: Signed distance from a rotating supporting hyperplane to the other ellipsoid used as a CBF (proved equal to true inter-ellipsoid distance); distributed CBF-QP safety filter on SE(2)/SE(3), extended to nonholonomic vehicles.
evaluation: MATLAB simulations: 2 ellipses, 1 robot vs obstacle (baseline: discriminant-based CBF of [13], qualitative), 16 ellipsoids (no baseline), 2 bicycle vehicles; QP solve 1-2 ms on Intel i7-10700 (quadprog).
contribution: Distributed CBF-QP collision avoidance for multiple ellipsoidal rigid bodies whose rotating supporting-hyperplane barrier recovers the exact separation distance, removing conservatism of prior ellipsoid CBFs.
flag: v1.5: mostly qualitative, baseline comparison qualitative only. Borderline: classical geometric CBF; multi-agent is a genuine distributed collision-avoidance setting but the contribution is the barrier geometry, not deferral/latency. Simulation only, mostly qualitative evaluation.

title: Combinatorial Control Barrier Functions: Nested Boolean and p-Choose-r Compositions of Safety Constraints
venue: IEEE Control Systems Letters
evidence: Sec. III, Thm. 1 / Eq. 18: a QP safety filter minimises ||u - k_d||^2 subject to p primitive barrier conditions whose pivot is the r-th largest CBF value, enforcing exact p-choose-r and nested Boolean safety specifications; Sec. V applies it to 11 patrolling agents.
method: Combinatorial CBFs: sort primitive CBFs, use r-th largest as pivot, relax barrier conditions on the rest; exact safe set for p-choose-r and nested Boolean compositions with only p constraints; matrix-CBF extension.
evaluation: Simulation only: 11 single-integrator agents, two L-shaped regions each needing >=4 agents; one centralised QP with 132 constraints vs 5448 Boolean expansions; no baseline controller, no metrics, no solve times.
contribution: Combinatorial control barrier functions enforce exact p-choose-r and nested Boolean compositions of safety constraints with a constraint count linear in the primitives, demonstrated on an 11-agent patrolling task.
flag: v1.5: no metric or baseline; coverage not hazard. Multi-agent only nominally: demo constraint is team coverage (>=4 agents per region), not collision/hazard; centralised QP. Relevant mainly as compositional-safety-specification background (RQ4). Letter-length, no quantitative evaluation (consider E2 if evaluation standard is strict).

title: Decentralized Safe and Scalable Multi-Agent Control Under Limited Actuation
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
evidence: Sec. III-B: the NN policy is forward-propagated and, if a collision is predicted, a decentralised MPC-ICBF QP with a single log-sum-exp combined barrier constraint is invoked to enforce safety and input limits among neighbouring quadrotors; evaluated up to 1024 agents (Sec. IV).
method: Jointly learned permutation-invariant neural integral CBF and controller; lightweight decentralised MPC-ICBF safety filter triggered on predicted collision; momentum-gradient deadlock escape with feasibility projection.
evaluation: Simulation (empty, 10x10 m maze), 4-1024 quadrotors; baselines MARL [37][40][41], GCBF, MA-CBF; metrics collision-avoidance %, deadlocks, input violations, per-agent compute ms; AMD Ryzen 2.9 GHz 8-core, no GPU named.
contribution: Decentralised neural integral CBF with an on-demand MPC safety filter and gradient-based deadlock escape achieves 100% collision avoidance under actuation limits, generalising from 16 training agents to 1024.
flag: Strong fit for (c). Counts of MPC-ICBF triggers (Table I) are a proxy for intervention rate (RQ5). Minor inconsistencies noted: gamma 0.8 vs 0.99; Fig. 6 caption seconds vs text ms. 'Real-time' claimed but no deadline or edge hardware.

title: Decentralized Uncertainty-Aware Multi-Agent Collision Avoidance With Model Predictive Path Integral*
venue: 2025 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
evidence: Sec. V-A/V-B: each robot embeds probabilistic ORCA collision constraints and control-limit chance constraints into the MPPI sampling distribution via an SOCP (LP for differential drive), using only its own noisy local observations; combined safety probability delta_o*delta_v*delta_u.
method: Decentralised MPPI whose sampling mean/covariance are adjusted by SOCP to satisfy chance-constrained ORCA (observation noise via inflated radius) and control-limit constraints under execution noise.
evaluation: C++ simulation: Circle 2-15 and Random 5-25 diff-drive robots, Gaussian observation/execution noise; baselines ORCA-DD, B-UAVC, MPPI-ORCA; metrics success rate, collisions, makespan (proposed 100%/0%); Gazebo 10 TurtleBot3 in ROS2 Nav2 at >10 Hz; hardware unspecified.
contribution: Decentralised uncertainty-aware MPPI embeds chance-constrained ORCA collision constraints into the sampling step via SOCP, reaching 100% success without collisions under noisy sensing and execution in dense multi-robot simulations.
flag: Constraints are baked into the planner rather than a separate interception layer, so (a) not claimed. '>10 Hz real-time' asserted without compute times or hardware. Simulation/Gazebo only.

title: Deep Equivariant Multi-Agent Control Barrier Functions
venue: 2025 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
evidence: Sec. IV-A/V: a learned, graph-based distributed CBF certificate h_phi is trained to satisfy the CBF condition over each agent's neighbourhood so that a swarm of N quadrotors reaches formation targets while avoiding inter-robot and obstacle collisions; 8-robot training transfers zero-shot to 512 robots.
method: Equivariant (SE(3)-subgroup) graph neural CBF and policy; policy imitates a centralised CBF-QP during training; distributed inference on local neighbourhood graph; no runtime QP filter.
evaluation: Simulated quadrotor swarms 8-512 robots, with/without obstacles; baselines GCBF, GCBF+, cCBF-QP, dCBF-QP; safe/reach/success rate, mean cost; AMD EPYC 7313P + A100; no timings reported.
contribution: Adds symmetry (equivariance) constraints to graph-based learned control barrier certificates so multi-robot safety policies trained on 8 quadrotors transfer zero-shot to swarms of 512.
flag: Safety enforced by training (learned certificate), not by a runtime interception layer, so (a) is borderline; simulation only, no latency figures; builds directly on GCBF+ (2401.14554, same batch); EGCBF+ row of Table I garbled in HTML source.

title: Distributed Resilience-Aware Control in Multi-Robot Networks
venue: 2025 IEEE 64th Conference on Decision and Control (CDC)
evidence: Sec. IV/Eq. 19: each robot solves a local CBF-QP that modifies its desired control only when the degree (resilience) constraint or the inter-robot collision constraint h_ij = Delta_ij^2 - Delta_d^2 would otherwise be violated, guaranteeing resilient consensus despite up to F misbehaving robots sending false information.
method: Distributed CBF-QP safety filter combining a neighbour-count CBF (sufficient condition for W-MSR resilient consensus in time-varying networks) with pairwise collision CBFs, using only local state and neighbours' reported values.
evaluation: Single 2D simulation: 11 single-integrator robots, F=2 malicious, three false-reporting cases; no baseline controller; metrics are CBF values, formations and consensus trajectories; no hardware or compute time.
contribution: Distributed CBF-based controller that keeps each robot above a resilient-consensus neighbour threshold while avoiding collisions, tolerating misbehaving robots that broadcast false state information.
flag: v1.5: single scenario, no baseline or ablation. Evaluation is a single simulated scenario with no baselines or timings (thin but present, so not E2); attacks are informational only, misbehaving robots assumed not to collide; hazard is network partition/consensus failure rather than physical.

title: Dynamic Collision Avoidance Using Velocity Obstacle-Based Control Barrier Functions
venue: IEEE Transactions on Control Systems Technology
evidence: Sec. III-B/III-D and Table III: velocity-obstacle-based CBF constraints are enforced as hard constraints in a per-step (0.05 s) QP while CLF navigation constraints are relaxed; a decision network replaces the MIQP so average solve time drops from 63-478 ms to 9.6-10.8 ms, which the authors describe as ensuring real-time performance.
method: Velocity-obstacle CBFs (no high-order CBFs) for acceleration-controlled unicycles; CLF-VOCBF mixed-integer QP, decomposed into QPs with LP feasibility check; learned decision network selects the avoidance side so one QP is solved per step.
evaluation: Simulation, single robot with static/moving circular obstacles plus qualitative multi-robot circle scenario; baselines HOCBF and classical VO; deadlock/completion/infeasible rates (600 tests), reach time, solve time (ms); Intel i9-13900HX CPU, RTX 4060 for training.
contribution: Velocity-obstacle-based control barrier functions with a learned decision network cut dynamic collision-avoidance QP solve times to about 10 ms while outperforming high-order CBFs against fast, close obstacles.
flag: v1.5: single-robot; multi-robot extension qualitative only. Borderline E4: primarily single-robot; multi-robot extension (Sec. IV-D) is qualitative with no metrics or robot count. (d) rests on reported solve times and a 'real-time' claim, not an explicit deadline; laptop CPU, no embedded deployment. Mild (c) via moving obstacles and reciprocal-VO multi-robot variant.

title: GCBF+: A Neural Graph Control Barrier Function Framework for Distributed Safe Multiagent Control
venue: IEEE Transactions on Robotics
evidence: Sec. III-IV: graph control barrier functions (GCBF) over each agent's local neighbourhood graph certify collision-free operation among N agents and obstacles; Remark 3 proves one GCBF certifies safety for any N, and Sec. VI reports >80% safety with >1000 agents and hardware tests on up to 8 Crazyflie drones.
method: Graph-attention GNN jointly learns a GCBF and a distributed policy (NN plus nominal LQR/PID) imitating a training-time centralised CBF-QP; finite-horizon rollout labelling handles actuator limits; LiDAR point-cloud input; no online QP.
evaluation: Five simulated dynamics envs, 8 train agents, tests to 1024 agents/128 obstacles; baselines GCBFv0, InforMARL, distributed MPC, centralised/decentralised CBF-QPs; safety/reach/success rate; i7-13700KF + RTX 3090, ~3 h training; Crazyflie 2.1 hardware, off-board controller at 50 Hz.
contribution: GCBF+ learns a single graph neural control barrier function and distributed policy that scale from 8 training agents to 1024 agents with higher safety and goal-reaching than hand-crafted CBF and multi-agent RL baselines.
flag: Journal extension of GCBF (CoRL 2023, arXiv 2311.13014) which may be queued separately. Safety is baked into the learned policy with no runtime filter, so (a) not claimed. Controller runs off-board at 50 Hz, no per-step latency figure, so no edge cell. Five dynamics environments are not cross-domain in the gap-matrix sense.

title: GIANT - Global Path Integration and Attentive Graph Networks for Multi-Agent Trajectory Planning
venue: 2025 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
evidence: Non-communicating decentralized collision avoidance for differential-drive robots framed as a POMDP; no safety filter, CBF or override: collisions are only penalised in the reward (r_collision = -25, Table I/Eq. 6, Sec. IV).
method: Decentralized PPO navigation policy per robot: A* global path integration plus graph-attention encoder over tracked LiDAR clusters of other agents; collision/social-distance reward shaping.
evaluation: VMAS simulation, 5-40 agents (circle, doorway, corridor, random); baselines NH-ORCA, DRL-NAV, GA3C-CADRL; success, collision/stuck, extra-time, speed; no hardware or inference-time reported.
contribution: Learned decentralized multi-robot navigation that fuses global A* paths with attentive graph encoding of neighbours, improving success rates in dense crowds over ORCA and DRL baselines.
flag: Borderline (c): multi-agent collision avoidance, but it is a navigation planner with no hazard detection, interception or safety layer; no latency/hardware data; no human element.

title: Gradient Field-Based Dynamic Window Approach for Collision Avoidance in Complex Environments
venue: 2025 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
evidence: Candidate trajectories 'that result in a collision' get infinite cost and are discarded each cycle; multi-robot extension treats other robots' predicted trajectories as GPDF obstacles (Sec. II-A, III-C).
method: Dynamic Window Approach with Gaussian-process distance-field obstacle cost plus gradient-direction penalty; infeasible (colliding) candidates pruned; distributed fleet extension via predicted neighbour trajectories.
evaluation: Simulation only: 5 single-robot non-convex scenarios vs MPC, DDPG, DWA (success rate); 4-robot intersection and 2-robot corridor vs DWA (success, time steps); no hardware or timing.
contribution: Gradient-field DWA that scores candidate velocities by GP distance-field value and gradient, improving collision-free navigation around non-convex obstacles and small robot fleets.
flag: Multi-agent only in a two-test extension; collision-cost pruning is a standard planner feasibility check, not a safety reflex or monitor; no latency numbers despite 'efficiency' claim.

title: Hierarchical LLMs in-the-Loop Optimization for Real-Time Multi-Robot Target Tracking Under Unknown Hazards
venue: 2025 IEEE International Symposium on Multi-Robot and Multi-Agent Systems (MRS)
evidence: Task-LLM assignments are verified before use: 'If beta(A) > 0, then the constraints are not met and we will skip the current output' (Sec. III-C.2); human supervisor input is 'optional ... and only triggered' when comments exist (Sec. III-E); robots track targets under sensing/communication danger zones (Sec. III-B).
method: Hierarchical bi-level optimisation for multi-robot target tracking: outer task-LLM assigns targets, inner action-LLM tunes objective weights; LLM outputs filtered by constraint checks; optional human supervisor feedback.
evaluation: Sim (2-8 robots/targets, GPT-3.5/4o) vs no-LLM and LLM+human: trace, sensing/comm attacks, path length; hardware 2 Dragonfly MAVs + 2 Scarab targets; LLM via hosted API, no latency measured.
contribution: Hierarchical LLM-in-the-loop optimisation for multi-robot target tracking under unknown danger zones, with constraint-checked LLM outputs and optional human supervisor feedback that reduces hazard exposures.
flag: v1.5: safety element incidental to tracking task; hazards are static adversarial zones. Borderline: hazards are adversarial danger zones in a tracking task, not agent-induced failures; LLM output verification is a simple feasibility skip, not a safety monitor; 'real-time' claim has no measured latency (LLM updates every 5-30 s); human role is advisory rather than takeover.

title: Homotopy-aware Multi-agent Navigation via Distributed Model Predictive Control
venue: 2025 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
evidence: Distributed MPC enforces pairwise inter-agent collision constraints (MBVC-WB) and safe-corridor obstacle constraints with a deadlock-resolution scheme; local optimisation solved in ~9.1 ms per interval for 8 agents (Sec. III-E, IV).
method: Homotopy-aware distributed MPC: each agent plans a global path with passage-time maps shared over ROS, soft coordination costs, triggered online replanning, and MPC trajectory optimisation with linear collision constraints.
evaluation: 20 random 8-agent obstacle maps x10 runs vs A*+MPC, OptMAPF+MPC, FastMAPF+MPC: scenario/swarm success, length, time (90.5% vs <=13%); 8 Crazyflies with OptiTrack; i7-13700K, 3.1 ms global / 9.1 ms local.
contribution: Distributed homotopy-aware MPC for multi-agent navigation that coordinates passage choices through shared time maps and online replanning, raising success in cluttered swaps from under 13% to over 90%.
flag: Borderline (c)/(d): multi-agent collision constraints and millisecond compute times reported, but it is coordination/planning with no hazard detection, interception or explicit latency constraint; central computer, no edge deployment.

title: Hybrid Decision Making for Scalable Multi-Agent Navigation: Integrating Semantic Maps, Discrete Coordination, and Model Predictive Control
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
evidence: Sec. II-C/II-D: areas can only be entered by agents that have claimed them and interfaces to non-reserved areas become inactive MPC constraints, eliminating inter-agent collision constraints while anticipating and avoiding deadlocks between agents.
method: Shared semantic graph map, discrete one-agent-per-area claim policy (Algorithm 1) reconfiguring per-agent MPC at each interface crossing; coordination baked into planning constraints, no runtime filter.
evaluation: PyBullet, 3-12 agents, 50 runs/scenario vs prior method [5] and no-cooperation; success/infeasible/collision rate, MPC solve 53-74 ms, cycle 66-119 ms at 5 Hz on i7-14700K; 2 ROSbot 2 PRO.
contribution: Claim-based area reservation decouples multi-robot coordination from MPC motion planning, removing inter-agent collision constraints and giving 0% collisions and 0% deadlocks for up to 12 robots at ~11 ms coordination overhead.
flag: v1.5: coordination policy; safety outcome secondary to scalable navigation. Borderline c vs E1 (protocol v1.2): mechanism is a coordination/mutual-exclusion policy whose safety effect (collisions, deadlocks) is reported as a metric; no runtime monitor; timing reported but no explicit latency constraint beyond IPOPT max_cpu_time 0.15 s; physical test only 2 robots; no human-in-the-loop.

title: Hybrid Safety Verification of Multi-Agent Systems using ψ-Weighted CBFs and PAC Guarantees
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Robotics (ICAR)
evidence: Sec. IX-A: at each time step the control input for all agents is computed by solving a constrained QP that minimizes instantaneous control effort while satisfying all pairwise safety constraints; Sec. VII-VIII derive a PAC bound on margin-aware safety violations from Monte Carlo rollouts.
method: Pairwise control barrier functions augmented with a psi-weighted directional control-coupling term, enforced as a runtime QP safety filter; offline empirical-Bernstein PAC certificate from Monte Carlo rollouts under bounded noise.
evaluation: Simulation, N=2 and 3 control-affine agents, bounded noise 0.01-0.05, 100x50 rollouts; empirical violation rate, Bernstein vs Hoeffding vs scenario bounds, psi sweep; CVXPY on Ryzen 9950X, no timing reported.
contribution: Augments multi-agent control barrier functions with a directional control-alignment weight and pairs the runtime QP filter with a PAC-style probabilistic safety certificate from Monte Carlo rollouts under bounded disturbances.
flag: v1.5: violation rate but no baseline or ablation. Only 2-3 agents; no solve-time or latency data despite CBF real-time framing; psi value used in Table I not stated; Bernstein bound dominated by its constant term (~0.15); 'quantum-inspired' framing is metaphorical; no human-in-the-loop.

title: Mean-Field Control Barrier Functions: A Framework for Real-Time Swarm Control
venue: 2025 American Control Conference (ACC)
evidence: Sec. III: at each time step a QP projects the nominal policy onto the admissible set K_CBF (Eq. 20) so that the mean-field barrier H(s,rho)>=0 (MMD distance of the swarm density to an incoming object) is kept nonnegative for all time.
method: Mean-field control barrier functions: swarm modelled as a probability measure, barrier condition on d/ds H derived via calculus on measures, runtime QP projection of shared feedback policy onto safe set; one constraint instead of n^2 pairwise.
evaluation: Two 3D double-integrator simulations (obstacle avoidance, tracking, up to 200 agents) in Python/cvxpy; only metric is H(s) trace staying >=0; no baselines, no hardware or solve times.
contribution: Lifts control barrier functions to the space of probability measures so a swarm of any size is kept safe by a single runtime QP constraint rather than n^2 pairwise constraints.
flag: v1.5: one qualitative barrier-trace plot, no baseline. Borderline E2: evaluation is qualitative (one barrier-trace plot), no baselines, no timing despite 'real-time' framing; inter-agent collisions not addressed (only swarm-vs-object); c met only in the swarm-vs-obstacle sense; no human-in-the-loop.

title: Merry-Go-Round: Safe Control of Decentralized Multi-Robot Systems with Deadlock Prevention
venue: 2025 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
evidence: Sec. IV-A (Alg. 1): every control period each robot checks pairwise distance and predicted positions over horizon T against k_D*r_safe to flag deadlock candidates, while Sec. III-D enforces unrelaxed pairwise-distance CBF constraints in a runtime CLF-CBF QP.
method: Decentralized CLF-CBF QP safety filter on unicycle robots plus per-period deadlock prediction that forms or joins shared circular roundabouts (MGR mode) to restore forward progress.
evaluation: Simulation 16x16 m, up to 120 robots, 4 environments vs GCBF+, ORCA, CLF-CBF; success/arrival rate, makespan; <2 ms per robot per period on Ryzen 7 laptop; DJI RoboMaster hardware demo.
contribution: Decentralized multi-robot CBF safety filter with predictive pairwise deadlock detection and temporary roundabouts, scaling to 120 robots at under 2 ms per robot per control step.
flag: Borderline: core contribution is deadlock-prevention coordination; safety element is a standard CBF-QP runtime filter. No formal deadlock-freedom proof; hardware results deferred to supplementary material; collisions not reported as a metric.

title: MobiLLM: An Agentic AI Framework for Closed-Loop Threat Mitigation in 6G Open RANs
venue: MILCOM 2025 - 2025 IEEE Military Communications Conference (MILCOM)
evidence: Sec. II-D 'Guardrails': rule-based deterministic output checkers and JSON sanitizers filter hallucinated or malformed agent outputs, and humans validate mitigation scripts; Fig. 1/2 and Sec. II-C: configuration changes are applied only after mandatory human approval and the agent escalates to an operator when no valid plan can be built from the API library.
method: Three sequential LLM agents (ReAct, Gemini-2.5-Flash) for threat analysis, RAG-based MITRE FiGHT classification, and response planning executed via fixed human-vetted workflows with prompt, rule-based and human-approval guardrails.
evaluation: OpenAirInterface/OSC RIC testbed, 5 reproduced cellular attacks, 5 runs; no baselines; Top-3 0.94, Top-1 0.72, tool CCR 0.64; latency named as metric but no numbers; hardware not reported.
contribution: LLM multi-agent framework for closed-loop O-RAN threat mitigation in which fixed workflows, output checkers and a mandatory human approval gate bound what autonomous agents may execute.
flag: v1.5: guardrails/human gate are design features not the studied subject; no baselines. Borderline E1/E4: guardrails and human approval are design features, not the studied subject; agents form a pipeline rather than interacting multi-agent state. Abstract claims reduced response latency but no latency values are reported; one of five cases produced a flawed plan without stating whether a guardrail caught it.

title: Multi-Agent Obstacle Avoidance Using Velocity Obstacles and Control Barrier Functions
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
evidence: Sec. IV: each timestep a per-agent QP picks the control closest to the reference subject to a hard braking-distance CBF constraint (Eq. 18) and input saturation, while the VO constraint (Eq. 17) is relaxed via a penalized slack so it acts only as guidance.
method: Per-agent runtime QP that combines a slack-relaxed velocity-obstacle guidance term with a hard control barrier function safety constraint for multi-agent collision avoidance.
evaluation: MATLAB/Simulink3D, 2-12 second-order-integrator agents (10 runs each) and 4-8 car-like agents vs VO, RVO, hVO, OVVO; success rate, collisions, episode length; 4.9-6.2 ms per iteration, hardware unspecified.
contribution: Combines velocity-obstacle guidance with a hard control-barrier-function safety constraint in one per-agent QP, achieving zero collisions across 2-12 agents where VO and RVO baselines fail or collide.
flag: Simulation only, centralized with full knowledge of other agents; CBF guarantee inherited from cited work, no feasibility proof; car-dynamics case qualitative only.

title: PRIMER: Perception-Aware Robust Learning-Based Multiagent Trajectory Planner
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
evidence: Fig. 1 and Sec. II: each agent optimizes (or, for PRIMER, predicts) a trajectory, checks it against received trajectories, runs a delay check over a period and commits only if no conflict appears, otherwise reverting to the previous trajectory; the paper states NN planners 'do not inherently provide such guarantees' so all PRIMER outputs pass the Robust MADER deconfliction check before commitment.
method: Perception-aware decentralized asynchronous UAV planners PARM/PARM* (optimization) and PRIMER (imitation-learned NN), with Robust MADER runtime deconfliction and delay checks applied to committed trajectories.
evaluation: Simulation only, 1-3 agents with dynamic obstacles vs PARM/PARM*; compute time, success, FOV rate, constraint violations; PRIMER 0.8 ms single-agent and 109-140 ms multi-agent on i9-9900K desktop.
contribution: Imitation-learned multiagent UAV planner PRIMER runs up to 5614x faster than its optimization-based expert, with a runtime Robust MADER deconfliction check guaranteeing committed trajectories are collision-free.
flag: v1.5: safety check inherited from prior work; primary claim is planning speed. Safety check (Robust MADER) is inherited from prior work, not the paper's contribution; 5614x speedup is from the single-agent case (multi-agent 10-50x); desktop timings only, no edge or real-robot results; agent-count inconsistency (text says two, tables three).

title: Safe Decentralized Density Control of Multi-Robot Systems using PDE-Constrained Optimization with State Constraints
venue: 2025 IEEE International Symposium on Multi-Robot and Multi-Agent Systems (MRS)
evidence: Sec. III-A: each robot solves a CLF-CBF quadratic program whose barrier h_i (Eq. 4) keeps the neighbourhood density out of the danger area A; Proposition 1 gives a sufficient condition under which local barriers imply global safety.
method: Decentralized density control: robots as Gaussian PDFs under Fokker-Planck PDE; per-robot CLF-CBF QP with worst-case neighbour assumption and slack relaxation; local-to-global invariance proposition.
evaluation: 15-robot 2D simulation (Ryzen 5 5600, MOSEK, 0.003 s per robot per step) and 4 ModalAI Seeker quadcopters; no baselines; metrics: density error V, global/local barriers h.
contribution: Decentralized CLF-CBF density controller for multi-robot teams that keeps team density out of danger areas, with a local-to-global safety condition and quadcopter validation.
flag: Borderline (c): safety mechanism is multi-robot, but the hazard is a static environmental danger area, not inter-agent interaction; collision avoidance explicitly delegated to robot level (Sec. IV). Constraint baked into planning QP, not a runtime interceptor. Reported 3 ms/robot/step compute (desktop sim) may interest RQ1 as background.

title: Safe Decentralized Multi-Agent Control using Black-Box Predictors, Conformal Decision Policies, and Control Barrier Functions
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
evidence: Sec. IV-B/Alg. 1: at each step a QP finds the control closest to u_ref satisfying conformal CBF constraints C_hat_j (Eq. 5) for every sensed agent, with slack lambda updated online from observed prediction error (Sec. IV-A); task is pairwise collision avoidance with pedestrians in SDD scenes (Sec. V).
method: Runtime CBF-QP safety filter whose constraint tightness lambda is adapted by online conformal decision theory to errors of a black-box trajectory predictor; long-run average loss bound (Thm. 3).
evaluation: Stanford Drone Dataset pedestrian scenes, virtual double-integrator robot, darts predictor; baselines pred/noLearn and gt/noLearn; metrics t_goal, collision frames, d_min; no hardware or timing reported.
contribution: Conformal decision theory adapts a decentralized CBF-QP safety filter to black-box predictor errors, trading collisions against goal time with a long-run average constraint-gap bound.
flag: No collision guarantee (authors state this, Sec. V); QP runs at higher rate than predictor but no latency numbers; minor inconsistencies between text and Table I (12 vs 13 collisions, eta=100 vs stated eta<=1 feasibility).

title: Safe Distributed Control of Multi-Robot Systems With Communication Delays
venue: IEEE Transactions on Vehicular Technology
evidence: Abstract/Sec. IV-A: a distributed CBF 'guarantees safety under local communication' for multi-robot collision avoidance; Sec. V/VI-A: a per-robot LSTM predictor estimates neighbours' current states from delayed messages and their Age-of-Information, trained alternately with a GNN controller.
method: Distributed CBF certificate; GNN controller and LSTM state predictor trained jointly with CBF hinge loss under Poisson communication delays with Age-of-Information; CBF not deployed online; heuristic switching variant.
evaluation: Simulation, 10 robots (single-integrator, Dubins), delays c_del 0.2-1.5 steps at Ts=0.03; baseline GNN without predictor and heuristic; metrics safety rate, trajectory length, goal distance; training RTX A4000 ~5 h; no runtime timing.
contribution: Distributed CBF with GNN controllers and an Age-of-Information-aware predictor restores multi-robot collision-avoidance safety that is otherwise lost under communication delays.
flag: Safety enforced via training loss, not runtime filter (Fig. 3: CBF model 'is not deployed in online operation'). Latency cell refers to communication delay/AoI, not inference latency. HTML truncated; details taken from PDF. Flag as journal extension if a conference version is queued.

title: Safe Human Robot Navigation in Warehouse Scenario
venue: 2025 IEEE 21st International Conference on Automation Science and Engineering (CASE)
evidence: Sec. IV-D: at each timestamp learned dynamics are rolled out for each discrete control candidate and 'any candidate with unsafe CBF values over the predicted future states is discarded before execution'; separate CBFs handle static obstacles, pedestrians and multi-robot pairs (Sec. IV-C), integrated with Open-RMF fleet coordination (Sec. V).
method: Neural CBFs (NCBF-BC, offline sparse labels) for static, pedestrian and robot-robot hazards; runtime rollout-and-discard filter over discrete controls with control-delay compensation; Open-RMF integration.
evaluation: Real hardware only: Freight, Jackal, Megarover, 1-4 robots, 0-2 pedestrians, 0.5-1.5 m/s, OptiTrack; no baselines; metrics collisions (0), min distance (>=0.7 m), mean velocity; onboard CPU, no GPU, no timing.
contribution: Learned control barrier functions filter unsafe control candidates at runtime so warehouse robot fleets under Open-RMF avoid static obstacles, pedestrians and each other without collisions in hardware tests.
flag: v1.5: hardware-only study with safety metrics but no baseline or ablation; maintainer may waive given real-robot evidence. Edge deployment is qualitative only (onboard CPU, no GPU, no per-cycle timing); no baselines; pedestrians present but no handoff/takeover (e not met). Minor inconsistencies on Megarover count and section cross-references.

title: Safe Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Behavior-Based Cooperative Navigation
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
evidence: Sec. IV-C: each robot's RL-proposed linear/angular velocities pass through a distributed nonlinear MPC safety filter that can override them at every time step, during both training and execution, penalising proximity to the two neighbours and the nearest obstacle.
method: Behaviour-based MARL steers a robot formation's centroid to a target; per-robot distributed NMPC (acados) filters RL actions for robot-robot and robot-obstacle safety at train and test time.
evaluation: Simulation (3 TurtleBot3; 1000 trials, S-paths, static/dynamic obstacles, 3-8 robots) and real robots (2 TB2 + 1 TB4); baselines MASAC, MADDPG, DMPC; success, collisions, timeouts, time, formation error; no latency/compute reported.
contribution: Shows a distributed MPC action filter can make multi-robot RL navigation collision-free in training and deployment while speeding convergence, with ablations quantifying the filter's incremental value.
flag: Safety filter is optimisation-based soft penalties, not hard constraints; no timing figures. v3 (Oct 2025) read via PDF; check for other queued versions.

title: SafeSwarm: Decentralized Safe RL for the Swarm of Drones Landing in Dense Crowds
venue: 2025 20th ACM/IEEE International Conference on Human-Robot Interaction (HRI)
evidence: Abstract claims a 'safe barrier net' and collision-free swarm landing, but the body (Sec. III) never defines the mechanism; safety appears only as reward penalties for obstacle collision (Eq. 1-6) and no collision metrics are reported.
method: Decentralised MAPPO policy for heterogeneous micro-drones landing on static/moving pads among static obstacles; safety via reward shaping (obstacle penalty, velocity scaling); mechanism named but undefined.
evaluation: gym-pybullet-drones sim (30 runs) vs reimplemented MARLander; real Crazyflie 2.1 flights (5) with Vicon; metrics landing success, cm error, landing time; no collision counts, no latency; training on i9/RTX4090.
contribution: Decentralised safe-RL swarm landing on moving pads among obstacles, validated on Crazyflie hardware, but the safety mechanism is undefined and collision outcomes are not reported.
flag: Borderline: nominally multi-agent safety, but mechanism is reward shaping only, no drone-drone collision term, no collision metrics, static obstacles; 'dense crowds' appears only as motivation. Could argue E2 (weak evaluation) instead.

title: Safety Guaranteed Robust Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Hierarchical Control for Connected and Automated Vehicles
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
evidence: Sec. IV-B / Alg. 1: a low-level MPC with robust control barrier functions computes the executed control u_safe from the high-level RMAPPO action, enforcing a speed-dependent ellipsoidal safe region around neighbouring vehicles under worst-case bounded observation noise.
method: Hierarchical Safe-RMM: robust MAPPO with worst-case Q-network picks discrete manoeuvres; robust CBF-constrained MPC enforces per-step inter-vehicle safety under bounded state uncertainty, in training and at test time.
evaluation: CARLA intersection and highway with 3 CAVs + 2-3 HDVs, 50 test episodes per condition; baselines Safe-MM, MCP (PID+CBF shield), MP, RULE; collisions and efficiency return; no hardware or compute time.
contribution: Combines robust MARL with a robust-CBF MPC execution layer so connected vehicles stay collision-free in mixed traffic under test-time observation noise, outperforming shielded and unshielded MARL baselines.
flag: Forward-invariance guarantee is cited from prior work, not proved here; robustness is to observation error, not timing; simulation only.

title: Safety-Critical and Distributed Nonlinear Predictive Controllers for Teams of Quadrupedal Robots
venue: IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters
evidence: Sec. III, Eq. 14: high-order CBF inequality constraints on robot-robot and robot-obstacle distances are embedded in each agent's local NMPC, which runs at 100 Hz with ~4.9 ms solve time (Sec. V-A); Theorem 1 gives forward invariance of the safe set.
method: Distributed NMPC per quadruped with embedded HOCBF collision constraints and a Lennard-Jones consensus term, exchanging predicted trajectories with one-step delay; whole-body QP tracks at 1 kHz.
evaluation: RaiSim sim (200 random terrains, 20 obstacles, 2 agents) vs LIP-DNMPC without CBF (66%) and WBC-level CBF (14.5%): 93.8% success; 2 Unitree A1 hardware tests (pushes, rough terrain); offboard Ryzen 7950X3D, 4.9 ms NMPC.
contribution: Embeds high-order control barrier functions in distributed NMPC so teams of quadrupeds plan long horizons collision-free at 100 Hz, raising success over barrier-free NMPC and low-level CBF shields.
flag: Safety is baked into the planner, not a runtime interceptor. Criterion (d) borderline: 10 ms loop with 4.9 ms solve reported, but compute is an offboard desktop, not edge; the 27.89% figure in the abstract is not defined in the body. Hardware involvement is only two robots.

title: Trust-Aware Safe Control for Autonomous Navigation: Estimation of System-to-Human Trust for Trust-Adaptive Control Barrier Functions
venue: IEEE Transactions on Control Systems Technology
evidence: Sec. III-B: per-pedestrian CBF decay rate gamma_j = gamma_ini + delta*tau_j^lambda is set from estimated trust tau_j, so lower trust enforces a stricter barrier constraint inside the MPC (constraint 16g); authors state the discrete-time CBF 'can be used to guarantee safety' under conditions (14a)-(14b).
method: Camera-based system-to-human trust estimator (smartphone use, eye contact, pose fluctuation; EfficientNetV2) modulates per-pedestrian discrete-time CBF decay rates inside an MPC for a single autonomous vehicle.
evaluation: 2D numerical sims (SLSQP, <=2 pedestrians, horizon N_h up to 7) and CARLA with 100 ms latency; no baseline controller; qualitative distance/trust/path plots; hardware and solve time not reported.
contribution: Trust-adaptive control barrier functions tighten an autonomous vehicle's MPC safety constraints around pedestrians whose camera-estimated attentiveness is low, demonstrated qualitatively in CARLA.
flag: Single controlled agent; pedestrians are perceived obstacles, not agents, and 'multi-agent' appears only in the conclusion. Safety is a planning constraint, not a runtime interceptor; no latency numbers, no handoff; no baseline or quantitative metrics. Borderline (a) only via CBF shielding.

title: Work Smarter Not Harder: Simple Imitation Learning with CS-PIBT Outperforms Large-Scale Imitation Learning for MAPF
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
evidence: Sec. II.B.3: CS-PIBT 'post-processes the network's probabilities and uses PIBT as a collision shield to resolve 1-step collisions'; Sec. III.C: 'we do not apply CS-PIBT in training', so the shield intercepts colliding actions only at execution time.
method: Decentralised GNN (SageConv, 9x9 FoV, <=5 neighbours) imitation policy for MAPF whose per-step action distributions are post-processed by a PIBT collision shield (CS-PIBT) that resolves 1-step vertex/edge conflicts.
evaluation: 27 MovingAI maps, 8 held-out, up to 1000 agents, 2-min timeout; baselines EPH, EECBS, PIBT, CS-Naive; success rate, cost, runtime; CPU-only execution ~0.06 s/step for 1000 agents; V100 training 4-30 min.
contribution: Shows that a lightweight PIBT collision shield wrapped around a simple imitation-learned MAPF policy beats large-scale learned policies, and argues shields should be standard for learned multi-agent planners.
flag: Core contribution is a runtime collision shield for a learned multi-agent policy (criterion a/c) with ablation of shield vs naive shield (RQ5 relevant). Grid-world only; no edge hardware, no formal latency bounds, no human element; execution in Python without GPU.

title: CoDe : A Cooperative and Decentralized Collision Avoidance Algorithm for Small-Scale UAV Swarms Considering Energy Efficiency
venue: 2024 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
evidence: Sec. V 'Decentralized Execution': the Emergency Avoidance Scheme (EAS) predicts each UAV's distances to obstacles and neighbours at the next control loop, flags the actor's action infeasible if below the safeguard distance (Eq. 7), and 'will choose a feasible action close to the action selected by the actor model'; response time reduced 'by over 99%' vs E2Coop.
method: CTDE multi-agent actor-critic with a counterfactual credit-assignment advantage for decentralised UAV collision avoidance, plus an execution-time safeguard (EAS) that replaces predicted-unsafe actions with the nearest feasible sampled action.
evaluation: Authors' MACAEnv 2D simulator, 2-4 UAVs with 1-2 obstacles, 100 episodes; baselines COMA, Shapley, E2Coop, MACA-no-EAS; failure rate (2% vs 21% in 4U2O), energy, response time 3-7 ms vs 0.37-0.63 s; hardware unspecified.
contribution: Decentralised MARL collision avoidance for small UAV swarms with a one-step predictive execution-time safeguard, cutting failure rate and response time versus heuristic and MARL baselines in simulation.
flag: arXiv HTML and PDF both serve the earlier 'MACA' version; the v2 abstract (IROS 2024) retitles it CoDe with 'up to three drones' and an updated credit-assignment framing - the published version may differ in details. Response-time claims are simulation-only on unspecified hardware (no edge deployment); EAS has no fallback if no candidate is feasible; COMA 3U1O row duplicates 2U1O (likely table error). Criterion (d) is borderline: latency is a reported metric, not an explicit constraint.

title: Collaborative Manipulation of Deformable Objects with Predictive Obstacle Avoidance
venue: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
evidence: Sec. VI: a QP 'computes the closest control input to the nominal controller' subject to CBF constraints for collision, overstretching and proximity avoidance, using 3N+1 simultaneous PBD simulations for distance sensitivities; Table I: 'execution times remained below 10 ms, affirming the suitability for real-time applications'.
method: Runtime CBF-QP safety filter over a nominal proportional leader-follower controller for N velocity-controlled assistant robots holding a deformable object; collision distances and Jacobians predicted via perturbed position-based-dynamics simulations.
evaluation: Simulation only (ROS, PBD in C++, QP in Python) on i9-10885H laptop; rope/rod/fabric with 1-3 assistants and predefined leader paths; no baseline; tracking error, min obstacle distance, spacing; QP 8-9 ms, total <10 ms.
contribution: A CBF quadratic-program safety filter uses predictive deformable-object simulation to keep several collaborating robots collision-free and within stretch limits under 10 ms per step, in simulation.
flag: v1.5: no baselines; human leader is a fixed trajectory. Borderline: multi-robot (1-3 assistants) manipulating one object with a human-held/teleoperated leader, but the human is only a predefined exogenous trajectory (no handoff). Sub-10 ms claim is on a laptop, not edge hardware, and the paper reports a brief constraint violation (0.031 m < 0.05 m offset) from delays. No baselines or real robots - E2 if maintainer requires comparative evaluation.
